title: Strip both plates off a barbell in its rack
instruction: Strip the barbell: take both plates off it and stand each one in the plate holder on its own side, leaving the bar resting in the rack's hooks. Then let go of everything.
context: Unlike unloading an overhang in the right order (one arm can do that), no order is safe here: a bar in rack hooks balances only while both ends carry the same load, so both plates must come off together. Exercise trainers and gym staff (O*NET 39-9031.00) strip loaded bars this way.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Rack: two fixed dark rubber J-hook posts at x 28, y +7 and -7, each a 2 cm thick open cradle 3 cm between its lips, holding the bar's axis 10 cm above the table. Bar: aluminium, 2.5 cm across, 40 cm long along y, 70 g with its red collars (5.2 cm across, 0.5 cm thick, at 10 to 10.5 cm either side of the middle) and 3 cm sleeves out to its ends; it can slide about 2 cm in the hooks. Plates: two black rubber technique plates, 14 cm across, 2.5 cm thick, 300 g, with a 5 cm bore, hanging on the sleeves against the collars, centres at x 28, y +11.75 and -11.75, 1 cm below the bar's axis (top rim 16 cm up). Plate holders: two fixed rubber blocks at x 28, y +31 and -31, 9 x 7 cm, each with a 3 cm wide slot along x, 2 cm deep, with a flared mouth, in which a plate stands on its rim.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and photos. 0 if a bar end ever rose more than 1.5 cm above its seat, the bar ever rose 1.2 cm or moved 1.2 cm forward or back at a hook (out of its cradle), the bar ever slid 3 cm along y, or a plate's lowest point ever fell 3 cm while no gripper held it (these are never undone). Otherwise: 0.25 one plate is off the bar (centre 21.25 cm or more from the bar's middle) and standing in its holder while the other is still on the bar; 0.5 both plates are off the bar and the bar is seated in its hooks (within 1 cm of its start), but a plate is not standing upright (within 12 degrees) on its holder's slot floor; 0.75 both plates stand in their holders and the bar is seated, but a gripper is within 3 cm of a plate or the bar, or things are not still; 1.0 all of that, with grippers 3 cm clear and the bar and plates still within 1 mm for the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Hang a plate on each sleeve against its collar, lay the bar in both cradles, and set the two holders on their marked outlines.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (friction 0.5): the plates are rings of boxes around a real bore. The bar is short and light so that one plate a side overbalances it, as two or three heavy plates do on a full-size bar. Plates are 300 g, within the arms' clean payload. No contact force cap is enforced.
